sections.name: File setup, deleteInput
sections.title: Confirmation rule and imports
sections.what: Defines the rule that a deletion request must contain the word DELETE, with a message to show if it does not. It also brings in the error type and the repository.
sections.why: Likely reason: requiring a typed word guards against accidental or scripted deletion.
sections.watch_out: The rule is defined here, but deleteMyAccount does not enforce it, so every caller must check the word first.

sections.name: exportMyData
sections.title: Exporting a user's data
sections.what: Builds the downloadable copy of a user's data as one object with an export time and a format name. If the account does not exist, it returns a not-found error.
sections.why: Likely reason: the format name and time let whoever reads the file know which version it is.

sections.name: deleteMyAccount
sections.title: Deleting an account
sections.what: Passes the user ID to the repository, which performs the permanent delete.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the business step separate from the database work.
sections.watch_out: This function does not check the confirmation word or that the user exists, so it depends entirely on callers.

summary: Handles the rules for exporting a user's data and deleting their account.
purpose: Business rules for the export and delete account features.
why: Likely reason: keeps rules separate from database work and from the web layer.
how: 1. Export: load the user's records, return a not-found error if the user is missing, and add the export time and format name. 2. Delete: pass the user ID to the repository. 3. The confirmation word rule is defined here for callers to use.
inputs: A user ID. For deletion, the caller should supply the confirmation word DELETE.
outputs: For export, an object with the export time, format name and grouped records. For deletion, nothing.
risks: The delete step does not check the confirmation word, so any caller that skips that check can delete an account.
debug: If an account was deleted without confirmation, check the route that calls this function. If export says not found, the user row is missing.
